name: Example: Determining an Intercept of a Tangent or Normal Line to a Curve Given in Implicit Form
problem:
The equation $x^2-2x+y^2+4y=5$ represents a circle. The normal line at the point $\left(0, -5 \right)$ on the circle intersects the $x$-axis at the point $P.$ What are the coordinates of $P?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13947863/assets/b6c52a76654a4a545d356890d4deb04c74301e4091422a51e84551aeb3ec1152.png)
worked_solution:
First of all, we need to find the slope of the normal line at the point $(0,-5).$ Remember that the slope of the normal line, $m',$ is the negative reciprocal of the slope of the tangent line:

$$
m' = -\frac{1}{m}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we will calculate the derivative using implicit differentiation, assuming that $y = y(x).$

$$
\eqalign{
	\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} (x^2-2x+ y^2+4y)
	&=\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} (5)\[5pt]	
	
	\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} (x^2)-\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} (2x)+\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} (y^2)+\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} (4y)&=\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} (5)\[5pt]	
	
	2x-2+2y\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}+4\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}&=0\[5pt]	
	
	
	(2y+4)\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}&=2-2x\[5pt]	
	
	\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}
	&=\dfrac{2-2x}{2y+4}
	
}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at the point $\left(0,\,-5 \right)$ is 

$$
\eqalign{
	m
	&=\left(\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}\right)_{\left(0,\,-5 \right)}\[5pt]
	&=\left(\dfrac{2-2x}{2y+4}\right)_{\left(0,\,-5 \right)}\[5pt]
	&=\dfrac{2-2\cdot 0}{2\cdot (-5)+4}\[5pt]
	&=\dfrac{2}{-6}\[5pt]
	&=-\dfrac{1}{3} \, .
	
}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is $m'=-\dfrac{1}{m}=3.$ We can write the equation of the normal at the point $\left(0,\,-5 \right)$ as follows:

$$
\eqalign{
	y-y_1 &=m'\left(x-x_1 \right)\[5pt]
	y+5 &=3\left(x-0 \right)\[5pt]
	y&=3x-5
}
$$

Now, we just need to find where this normal line intersects the $x$-axis. At the point $P$ the $y$-coordinate is $0,$ so we set $y=0$ and solve for $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
	y&=3x-5\[5pt]
	0&=3x-5\[5pt]
	x&=\dfrac{5}{3}
}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $\left(\dfrac{5}{3},\,0 \right).$
